# S01 — Define the security contract and supported threat model

Agree and document what obfuscation protects, what it does not protect, and the supported attacker and workflow assumptions. Use this contract to guide cryptographic and operational changes.

**Findings:** README.md documents deterministic-token leakage and plaintext manifests; no recorded Slicer goals · **Size: S** · **Trees:** core, docs

**2026-09-28** — Security contract agreed: accidental-exposure risk reduction for controlled workflows; sharing is case-by-case. Docs cover retained structure and inference risk, manifest confidentiality, deterministic leakage, current compatibility, and no new crypto dependency.

## Why

The project currently has no recorded goals or shared statement of what obfuscation protects. README documents that manifests can contain plaintext mappings and deterministic tokens reveal equality and frequency. Security design and claims need an agreed boundary before further crypto work.

## Files

README.md; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md; Obfuscator/PackageReadme.md; relevant public API comments.

## Failing tests

No code regression is assumed. Record review cases: plain manifest behavior, passphrase-protected manifests, deterministic token equality leakage, and limits of reversibility.

## Implement

Document supported users and workflows, attacker assumptions, data the tool protects, data it does not protect, manifest confidentiality, token leakage, and the distinction between obfuscation and encryption. Record compatibility constraints and approved dependency posture.

## Check

Review statements against current code and tests. Ensure all three readmes describe the same guarantees and do not claim cryptographic secrecy from obfuscation alone.
